todo_line: - [ ] 004 Implement and test explicit custom-group-removal follow cleanup through public Messaging APIs, including manual and auto-follow sources, idempotent stale-safe remove/re-add ordering, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behaviour.
outcome: Finish task 004 by making removal ordering durable even when an older cleanup preserves a newer follow or a pre-removal send creates its conversation after cleanup acknowledgement, and by making reply auto-follow contingent on successful reply acceptance.
scope: Revise the current task-004 candidate in place and retain its Club-owned membership generations, public `Memba.Membership.Policies.ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` to `Memba.Messaging` boundary, projection checkpoint barrier, effective-access-union check, idempotent Messaging facts, and custom-group add/remove completion contract.

Correct `Memba.Messaging.ConversationFollowers.execute/2` for cleanup generation 5 against current follow generation 6: preserve the newer follow while durably recording cleanup ID/cutoff 5. After an ordinary user unfollow removes generation 6, delayed manual, root-sender, or reply-author follow work at generation 4 must still be rejected rather than restoring pre-removal state.

Make an acknowledged removal cutoff apply to relevant conversation streams created later. A root send authorized/prepared at an older generation and dispatched only after `clear_removed_group_member_follows/2` completes must not create a fresh stale auto-follow merely because the cleanup's one-time conversation enumeration could not see that stream. Use a durable person/removal cutoff or an equivalent event-sourced ordering mechanism through public Messaging APIs; do not rely on a transient process cache or direct projection mutation.

Change `Memba.Messaging.post_message_reply/2` orchestration so reply-author auto-follow is established only if the `PostMessageReply` command is accepted. Blank, duplicate-message-id, or otherwise rejected replies must emit neither `ConversationFollowed` nor effective follow state. Audit `post_inbound_club_message_reply/5`, which uses the same pre-dispatch helper, and keep all reply entry points on the same success-only rule. Preserve successful reply dispatch return values, generation ordering, recipient behavior, and deterministic projection replay.

Add focused deterministic tests for both ordering holes and reply rejection. Cover cleanup 5 -> follow 6 preserved -> ordinary unfollow -> delayed generation-4 manual/root/reply work rejected; a pre-removal root send dispatched after cleanup acknowledgement; and rejected blank plus duplicate (or equivalent aggregate-rejected) replies leaving no follow fact/state.

Complete the packet-required dispatch-option matrix with explicit list-based consistency and every supported caller-selected Commanded return shape used by these APIs: `returning: :aggregate_state`, `:aggregate_version`, `:events`, `:execution_result`, and `false`, plus `include_execution_result` and `include_aggregate_version`. Prove public custom-group add/remove calls still wait for durable cleanup where promised and return the selected shape. Retain existing default, `:strong`, `:eventual`, event-free exact-retry, and `{:ok, result}` unfollow coverage.

Keep and rerun the existing focused proof for manual/root/reply follow sources, historic absent-generation replay, delayed first cleanup, shared/unrelated access, projection lag, idempotency, and direct Everyone/Admin no-ops; adjust only where the corrected event contract requires it.
scope_exclusions: Do not replace task 004 with a new task or reset its revision identity. Both prior candidate origins remain cumulative and unresolved until review accepts this obligation.

Do not change task 001's accepted removal authorization, actor/target validation, self/last-member behavior, club role/membership preservation, system-group rejection, or `GroupMemberRemoved`-only transition semantics except for backward-compatible task-004 ordering data.
Do not implement broader group/conversation read or action authorization, queued-delivery/provider-handoff reauthorization, or open-LiveView refresh assigned to tasks 009-011.
Do not add Leave/Remove UI, confirmations, shared member-row changes, post-removal screens, or empty-group UI behavior assigned to tasks 012-014.
Do not edit iteration-064 feature files or implement the browser/domain acceptance layer assigned to tasks 015-016.
Do not mutate Membership projections from Messaging or Messaging projections from Membership. Preserve the separate bounded contexts and coordinate through public APIs and durable commands/facts.
Do not redesign unrelated delivery, conversation authorization, multi-group editing, projection infrastructure, or club role lifecycle.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, browser acceptance, or another unscoped full-suite command; task 017 and the deterministic `dev_check` node own the final repository gate.

references.facts: Implementation Plan 2 and the acceptance/open-technical-decision text require public Messaging APIs, idempotent facts, all manual/root/reply follow sources, stale remove/re-add safety, unrelated-follow preservation, and unchanged system-group behavior.

Iteration 062 established the origin-replaying Membership-to-Messaging cleanup collaboration and requires departure/rejoin ordering; task 004 extends that same collaboration to explicit custom-group removal.
Membership owns group membership and Messaging owns follow state. Coordination uses public context APIs rather than another context's aggregates or projection storage.
The Club stream is authoritative for membership lifecycle and preserves historic facts; system-group membership remains a downstream policy consequence.

`execute/2` currently returns `[]` when cleanup generation is older than the current follow, so no `ConversationUnfollowed` records that cleanup ID/cutoff. An ordinary unfollow later deletes the newer follower generation, allowing delayed older follow work to apply.

`clear_removed_group_member_follows/2` currently enumerates `list_conversations_for_group/1` only once, leaving later-created streams without the removal cutoff. `post_message_reply/2` and `post_inbound_club_message_reply/5` call `establish_reply_follow/2` before dispatching `PostMessageReply`, so aggregate rejection can leave a follow.

`Message.execute/2` is the authoritative acceptance boundary for `PostMessageReply`, including blank-body and duplicate-message rejection. Follow establishment must be causally downstream of successful acceptance.

The public custom-group add/remove paths preserve Commanded consistency and returning options while waiting on durable cleanup progress. Extend tests without regressing default, eventual, event-free retry, or selected return shapes.

The strong origin-replaying handler carries Club-owned membership generation, event identity, and checkpoint into the public Messaging cleanup API. Preserve origin replay and system-group no-op behavior.

The existing older-cleanup test asserts only `[]` and preservation of generation 5; it does not apply a durable cutoff, ordinarily unfollow the newer state, then prove delayed generation-4 manual/root/reply work remains rejected.

Existing generation and suspended-handler tests create known conversations before manual cleanup handling. Add a send whose conversation stream is first created after cleanup acknowledgement, plus explicit-list consistency and caller-returning coverage.

Current rejection tests assert no reply projection but do not assert absence of `ConversationFollowed` facts/effective follow state. Add negative assertions for blank and duplicate or another aggregate-rejected reply.
Successful root and reply `MessageSent` auto-follow projection behavior must remain deterministic after reply orchestration changes.
Commands and aggregate events remain the write authority; read projections may lag and must not become the source of the ordering invariant.
Ordering and replay behavior must be represented by durable, backward-compatible facts rather than ephemeral workflow memory.
Use focused tests and deterministic synchronization such as supervised processes, monitors, `Task.yield/2`, handler suspension, or state barriers rather than sleeps.

constraints: Keep task identity 004 and revise the existing candidate; do not invent another task for the same rejected obligation.

Use Club-owned membership history as the causal source and Messaging-owned event-sourced state as the follow authority. Do not query another context's aggregate internals or directly write projection tables.
Recording an older cleanup must not hide or unfollow a genuinely newer follow. It must only preserve the cutoff needed to reject work at or before that removal generation.

The late-conversation solution must survive process restart/replay and apply before stale root/reply/manual follow establishment can become authoritative; a post-enumeration projection sweep alone is insufficient.
Ordinary user unfollow semantics remain distinct from membership-removal cleanup. A later valid follow above the durable cleanup cutoff must still be possible.
Reply auto-follow must reflect a successfully accepted reply and remain authoritative for reply-only authors; do not solve rejection leakage by dropping reply auto-follow coverage.
Preserve backward replay of historic `GroupMemberAdded`, `GroupMemberRemoved`, `MessageSent`, `ConversationFollowed`, and `ConversationUnfollowed` shapes with absent generation/order fields.
Preserve `ClearRemovedGroupMemberFollows` origin replay while ensuring ordinary projector reset/replay does not dispatch cross-context side effects.

Preserve successful application-service return semantics for default and all supported caller-selected Commanded return options while honoring cleanup completion for `:strong`, `:eventual`, and explicit handler lists.
Limit edits to durable cleanup/follow ordering, reply-follow success orchestration, completion-option coverage, and their focused tests. Leave tasks 009-017 untouched.
completion_evidence_required: List changed paths and describe the durable ordering facts/state used both for per-conversation cutoffs and conversations first created after cleanup acknowledgement, including replay and historic absent-field semantics.
Report exit statuses and test counts for both focused test commands on the exact handoff state, plus `git diff --check`.

Identify a test proving cleanup generation 5 preserves current follow generation 6, records its cutoff, survives an ordinary unfollow, and rejects delayed generation-4 manual, root-auto, and reply-auto follow work.

Identify a deterministic test where cleanup is acknowledged before an older authorized/prepared root send first creates its conversation stream, and show the stale sender auto-follow never becomes effective.

Identify tests proving blank and duplicate or otherwise aggregate-rejected replies emit no reply and no follow fact/state, while successful reply auto-follow and caller-selected return values still work.

Show explicit handler-list consistency and all supported caller-selected return shapes (`:aggregate_state`, `:aggregate_version`, `:events`, `:execution_result`, `false`, `include_execution_result`, and `include_aggregate_version`) for public add/remove, alongside retained default, `:strong`, `:eventual`, event-free exact-retry, and successful `{:ok, result}` unfollow handling.
Show existing manual/root/reply source cleanup, first delayed removal, shared/unrelated access, projection-lag, idempotency, legacy replay, and Everyone/Admin no-op tests still pass.

Confirm accepted task-001 behavior remains unchanged: explicit removal emits only the reusable Membership removal fact for a transition, exact retry emits no new fact, and club membership/roles plus system-group guards are preserved.

latest_review.summary: Durably record an older cleanup cutoff without hiding a newer follow; protect conversation streams created only after cleanup acknowledgement; establish reply auto-follow only after successful reply acceptance; and add explicit-list consistency plus caller-selected return-mode coverage.

latest_worker_result.summary: The candidate added Club membership generations, generation-bearing manual/root/reply follow facts, cleanup cutoffs, durable handler checkpoint waiting, successful Messaging return normalization, system-group no-op coverage, and reported 35- and 41-test focused suites passing; the latest review found the remaining ordering and reply-rejection gaps described above.
